key_insight: GSMR3D uses one model per MRI contrast to reconstruct varied 3D resolutions, preserving tumour-relevant information without separate models for each acquisition geometry.
clinical_relevance: The approach could support shorter brain MRI acquisitions while retaining information useful for tumour segmentation and metastasis detection; it is imaging research, not cancer drug discovery.
method: Represents MRI volumes with learned anisotropic 3D Gaussian prototypes.
Uses scale-conditioned frequency encoding for arbitrary isotropic and anisotropic reconstruction.
Applies an exact measurement-consistency projection to match acquired low-resolution data.
evidence_signal: Trained on 3,731 contrast-enhanced T1 and 30,254 T1 brain MRI volumes, GSMR3D improved perceptual metrics across evaluated geometries and achieved the highest lesion sensitivity on an independent brain-metastasis cohort.
watch_item: Specialist models retained higher PSNR in anisotropic settings, and downstream task results do not establish prospective clinical benefit.
paper_title: Arbitrary-Scale Anisotropic 3D MRI Super-Resolution with Gaussian Prototypes
